title: Movie Watchlist API
tagline: Saves nothing, deletes nothing, and the rate limiter is never wired in.
ticket:
**WATCH-212 · Watchlist endpoints broken after refactor**

QA reports that the watchlist feature silently does nothing. Users click **Add**, see a success toast, but the movie never shows up. Removing returns success even for movies that were never added. The mobile team also says `/check/:movieId` returns an array instead of a flag.

Product additionally requires **rate limiting**: a user may add/remove at most **10 times in a rolling 2-minute window**; the 11th call must get **429**. A teammate started a limiter in `middleware/rateLimiter.js` but it was never finished.

**Definition of done:** all tests in `tests/watchlist.test.js` pass. Don't edit the tests.

bugs.title: addToWatchlist never writes to the DB
bugs.explain: It validates the movie then sends 201 without calling `Watchlist.create`. There is also no duplicate check, so a second add also gets 201 instead of 400.

bugs.title: remove uses find() instead of a delete
bugs.explain: `find()` only reads. Use `findOneAndDelete({ user, movie })` and send **404** with the exact message the test expects when it returns `null`.

bugs.title: check status returns an array under the wrong key
bugs.explain: `find()` always resolves to an array (`[]` is truthy!). Use `findOne` and `!!entry`, and the key must be `inWatchlist`.

bugs.title: getWatchlist returns ids, not movies
bugs.explain: `item.movie` is just an ObjectId until you call `.populate('movie')` on the query.

bugs.title: limiter logic is inverted and crashes
bugs.explain: `windowMs` is undefined, the filter keeps *old* timestamps (`>=` should be `<`), `if (requests)` is always true for arrays, and `validRequests` doesn't exist.

bugs.title: limiter never mounted
bugs.explain: Create one limiter instance and put it between auth and the handler on `/add` and `/remove`. One shared instance means add+remove share the same counter.

hints: Run the tests first and group failures by file. Six tests, four root causes.
`await Model.find(...)` always resolves to an array. Arrays are truthy even when empty.
For the limiter: what is `windowMs` inside the inner function? Where is it defined?
Express runs route handlers left to right: `router.post('/add', auth?, limiter, handler)`.

title: Auth Service: Register, Login, JWT
tagline: Passwords stored in plain text and nobody can log in.
ticket:
**SEC-88 · P1 · Auth service regressions**

Security scan flagged that **passwords appear in plain text** in the users collection and that `/register` returns the password field in its response. Meanwhile support says **nobody can log in**, and users who registered with a capitalised email can't log in at all. Even freshly issued tokens are rejected by `GET /me`.

**Definition of done:** all tests in `tests/auth.test.js` pass. Keep the API contract unchanged.

bugs.title: pre('save') hook uses an arrow function
bugs.explain: Arrow functions don't get their own `this`, so `this` is not the document. Mongoose hooks and methods must be `function () {}`.

bugs.title: bcrypt.compare arguments reversed
bugs.explain: Signature is `compare(plainText, hash)`. Reversed, it's always false, so every login is 401.

bugs.title: password leaks in JSON
bugs.explain: Add a `toJSON.transform` that deletes `ret.password` (or `select: false` on the field).

bugs.title: email lookups are case-sensitive
bugs.explain: The schema lowercases on save, but queries use the raw input. Normalise with `.toLowerCase().trim()` before `findOne`.

bugs.title: token parsing + env var typo
bugs.explain: `'Bearer xyz'.split(' ')[0]` is `'Bearer'`, so take index 1. Also `JWT_SECRT` is a typo, so the secret is `undefined` and verify always throws.

hints: What is `this` inside an arrow function declared at module level?
Read bcrypt's signature carefully: which argument is the hash?
Log `process.env` keys. Is the variable you read actually set?
Schema `lowercase: true` transforms on save, not on your query input.

title: Inventory Stock & Error Handling
tagline: The error handler never runs and stock goes negative.
ticket:
**INV-431 · Overselling during peak-sale load test**

During the load test the warehouse dashboard showed **negative stock** for several SKUs, and the stock endpoint shows numbers that are always **one update behind**. Clients also report that bad input returns an **HTML 500 page** instead of our JSON error format.

Expected behaviour:
- `PATCH /api/products/:id/stock` returns the **new** document. If shipping would push stock below 0, respond **409** and leave stock untouched (it must be safe under concurrency).
- Malformed ids return **400** `{ message: 'Invalid product id' }`.

**Definition of done:** `tests/inventory.test.js` is green.

bugs.title: error handler has 3 parameters
bugs.explain: Express recognises an error handler **only** by arity 4: `(err, req, res, next)`. With 3 params it's treated as a normal middleware, so errors fall through to Express's default HTML 500.

bugs.title: CastError isn't mapped
bugs.explain: A malformed ObjectId throws `CastError` from Mongoose. Map it to 400.

bugs.title: findByIdAndUpdate returns the OLD document
bugs.explain: Mongoose returns the pre-update doc unless you pass `{ new: true }`.

bugs.title: no stock guard (and read-then-write is racy)
bugs.explain: Put the guard *inside* the update filter: `{ _id, stock: { $gte: needed } }`. That's atomic, so two concurrent orders can't both pass.

hints: Count the parameters of the error handler. How does Express tell an error handler apart?
What does findByIdAndUpdate return by default: the doc before or after?
Checking stock first and updating second is a race. Can the filter do the check?

title: Order History Pagination
tagline: Page 1 is empty, totals are wrong, the oldest orders show first.
ticket:
**ORD-77 · Order history page shows the wrong orders**

Customers opening *Your Orders* see an **empty first page** or random old orders. The pager says "1 of 1" even for customers with hundreds of orders. A partner integration also sent `limit=100000` and took down a replica.

Spec: newest first by `placedAt`; `page` is 1-based; `limit` defaults to 10 and is capped at 50; `page` and `limit` in the response are **numbers**; `total` counts all matching orders.

bugs.title: off-by-one page offset
bugs.explain: With 1-based pages, the skip is `(page - 1) * limit`. `page * limit` skips the whole first page.

bugs.title: query params are strings
bugs.explain: `req.query.page` is `'2'`, not `2`. Parse with `parseInt` and validate, falling back to defaults on NaN.

bugs.title: sort direction
bugs.explain: Newest first means descending: `{ placedAt: -1 }`.

bugs.title: total counts the page, not the collection
bugs.explain: Use `countDocuments(filter)`. You can run it in parallel with the page query via `Promise.all`.

bugs.title: no limit cap
bugs.explain: Clamp with `Math.min(MAX_LIMIT, …)`. `MAX_LIMIT` was declared but never used.

hints: Write out page 1 with limit 10 by hand: which indices should be returned?
typeof req.query.page?
Is `data.length` the number of orders or the number on this page?

title: Checkout Pricing Engine
tagline: Totals come back as strings and coupons give 1000% off.
ticket:
**CHK-19 · Customers charged wrong amounts**

Finance flagged quotes where a 10% coupon produced a **negative total**, tax was computed **before** the discount, and the mobile app crashed because money fields arrived as **strings** (`"48.60"`). A malformed request with `qty: "2"` was accepted too.

Pricing rules are documented at the top of `services/pricing.js`. Make the tests pass.

bugs.title: reduce without an initial value
bugs.explain: Without `0` as the seed, the first accumulator is the first *item object*, so you get `'[object Object]11'`-style garbage.

bugs.title: percent used as a fraction
bugs.explain: `percent: 10` means 10%, so divide by 100.

bugs.title: minSubtotal comparison
bugs.explain: `subtotal > undefined` is always false, so SAVE10 never applied, and 'at least 100' means `>=`. Default the minimum with `?? 0`.

bugs.title: tax base and string rounding
bugs.explain: Tax applies to `subtotal - discount`. `toFixed` returns a **string**, so round with `Math.round(n * 100) / 100`.

bugs.title: weak validation
bugs.explain: Reject empty carts and non-integer quantities. `'2' <= 0` is false, so string quantities slipped through.

hints: What is the accumulator on the first iteration of reduce with no seed?
What type does Number.prototype.toFixed return?
Compare `5 > undefined` in the console.

title: Product Page Response Cache
tagline: Every product page shows the same product, and the cache never caches.
ticket:
**CAT-512 · Product detail pages show the wrong item**

After adding a response cache to cut DB load, product pages started **crashing** or showing **another product's data**. Updated prices also stay stale.

Requirements: cache `GET /api/products/:id` per URL for **30 seconds**. A `PUT` to a product must invalidate its cached entry.

bugs.title: unbound res.json
bugs.explain: `const originalJson = res.json` loses `this`. Calling `originalJson(body)` throws because it runs with `this === undefined`. Use `res.json.bind(res)`.

bugs.title: cache key ignores the id
bugs.explain: `req.baseUrl` is `/api/products` for every product. Use `req.originalUrl`.

bugs.title: TTL check inverted
bugs.explain: It served entries only when they were *older* than the TTL. Fresh means `age < TTL`.

bugs.title: no invalidation on write
bugs.explain: Call `invalidate('/api/products/' + id)` after a successful update.

hints: Detaching a method from its object: what happens to `this`?
Log the cache key for two different product ids.
Write the freshness condition in words first.

title: Async/Await Pitfalls in a Task API
tagline: Responses go out before the database work finishes.
ticket:
**TSK-9 · Task API returns garbage and lies about results**

- `GET /api/tasks/:id` returns a strange object with `op` and `_sort` keys instead of the task.
- Bulk complete always reports `{ updated: 0 }`.
- Deleting a malformed id returns 204 and an *UnhandledPromiseRejection* shows up in the logs.

Make `tests/tasks.test.js` pass.

bugs.title: missing await on a Query
bugs.explain: A Mongoose Query object is always truthy. Without `await` you serialise the query itself. Validate the id up front for the 400 case.

bugs.title: async callback inside forEach
bugs.explain: `forEach` ignores returned promises, so the response is sent before any update resolves. Use `Promise.all(ids.map(...))` or a `for...of` with `await`.

bugs.title: try/catch can't catch an un-awaited promise
bugs.explain: Without `await`, the rejection happens after the try block has exited. Await it, then check for `null` and return 404.

hints: Log `typeof task.then` in getTask.
When does `res.json({ updated })` run relative to the awaits inside forEach?
A try/catch only catches what you await inside it.

title: Meeting Room Double-Booking
tagline: Two teams keep landing in the same room at the same time.
ticket:
**FAC-301 · Conference rooms double booked**

The booking API only rejects a new booking if it is entirely *inside* an existing one, so partial overlaps get through. Back-to-back meetings (10:00–11:00 then 11:00–12:00) must be **allowed**. Bookings where end ≤ start must be **400**. The listing must be sorted by start time.

bugs.title: wrong overlap predicate
bugs.explain: Intervals [s1,e1) and [s2,e2) overlap **iff** `s1 < e2 && s2 < e1`. As a query: `start: { $lt: newEnd }, end: { $gt: newStart }`. Strict inequalities allow back-to-back.

bugs.title: no start/end validation
bugs.explain: Parse the dates, reject invalid ones, and require `end > start`.

bugs.title: unsorted list
bugs.explain: `find()` has no guaranteed order. Add `.sort({ start: 1 })`.

hints: Draw the 5 overlap cases on a timeline. Which ones does the current query catch?
What is the negation of 'A ends before B starts OR B ends before A starts'?

title: Admin Panel Access Control
tagline: Unauthenticated users crash it; logged-in customers become admins.
ticket:
**SEC-140 · P0 · Privilege escalation in admin API**

Pen-test found that **any logged-in customer can call admin endpoints**. Anonymous calls return **500** instead of 401. Separately, an admin managed to **delete their own account**, locking the team out.

bugs.title: assignment instead of comparison
bugs.explain: `req.user.role = role` *sets* the role and is truthy, so everyone passes and becomes admin in memory. Use `===`.

bugs.title: middleware order
bugs.explain: `requireRole` runs before `requireAuth`, so `req.user` is undefined and you get a TypeError and a 500. Authenticate first, then authorise.

bugs.title: ObjectId compared with ===
bugs.explain: `req.user._id` is an ObjectId, `req.params.id` is a string, and `===` is never true. Use `.equals()` or compare `String()`s.

hints: Read requireRole character by character.
Which middleware populates req.user?
typeof req.user._id vs typeof req.params.id?

title: URL Shortener Service
tagline: The second link ever created crashes the service.
ticket:
**LNK-4 · Shortener fails after the first link**

Marketing can create exactly **one** short link; every later request returns 500. Clicks always show **0**, and browsers cache the redirect forever, which breaks link edits.

Spec: codes ≥ 6 chars; re-shortening an existing URL returns the **same code with 200**; redirects are **302**; each visit increments `clicks`.

bugs.title: substring(2, 2) is always empty
bugs.explain: Every code is `''`, so the unique index throws E11000 on the 2nd insert. Use `substring(2, 9)`.

bugs.title: `link.clicks + 1` is a no-op
bugs.explain: The expression is computed and thrown away. Better still, use an atomic `$inc` so concurrent clicks aren't lost.

bugs.title: 301 vs 302
bugs.explain: 301 is permanent and browsers cache it. Editable links need 302.

bugs.title: no idempotency for duplicate urls
bugs.explain: Look up an existing link by url first and return it with 200.

hints: What does 'abcdef'.substring(2, 2) return?
Is there an assignment in `link.clicks + 1`?
Which redirect status do browsers cache permanently?

title: Express Wiring & Route Order
tagline: Every endpoint answers 404 and /me is treated as a user id.
ticket:
**PLAT-3 · New users service returns 404 for everything**

A new microservice was scaffolded by an intern. Every request returns **404 "No route…"**, and when that was briefly hot-patched, `GET /api/users/me` blew up with a CastError and `POST` created users with no fields.

Fix the app wiring. Don't change the response formats.

bugs.title: 404 catch-all mounted before the routes
bugs.explain: Express matches in registration order. A middleware with no path matches **everything**, so it must come after all routers.

bugs.title: express.json() missing
bugs.explain: Without the body parser `req.body` is `undefined`, so `User.create(undefined)` fails validation.

bugs.title: `/:id` shadows `/me`
bugs.explain: `/:id` also matches `/me` (id = 'me' → CastError). Register static paths before parameterised ones.

hints: Express walks middleware/routes top to bottom. What matches first?
What is req.body without a body-parsing middleware?
Which route pattern does '/me' match first?

title: Product Search, Sorting & Injection
tagline: Searching 'c++' crashes, sorting is random, and sellers log in without a key.
ticket:
**SRCH-61 · Search 500s + security finding**

- Searching for `c++` or `(` returns **500**.
- Results are in a random order instead of highest rating first.
- The price filter widget shows `[100, 49, 9]` as "ascending".
- **AppSec:** `POST /api/sellers/login` accepts `{"apiKey": {"$ne": "x"}}` and logs the attacker in.

bugs.title: user input compiled as a regex
bugs.explain: `new RegExp('c++')` throws (`Nothing to repeat`) and `.` matches anything. Escape regex metacharacters first.

bugs.title: comparator returns a boolean
bugs.explain: `sort` needs a negative/zero/positive **number**. `a < b` returns true/false, which gives an engine-dependent order. Use `b.rating - a.rating`.

bugs.title: default sort is lexicographic
bugs.explain: `[100, 49, 9].sort()` compares strings, so `'100' < '49' < '9'`. Pass `(a, b) => a - b`.

bugs.title: NoSQL injection
bugs.explain: JSON bodies can contain objects. `{ $ne: 'x' }` turns the filter into 'any key that isn't x'. Validate that credentials are strings.

hints: What does `new RegExp('c++')` do?
What must an Array.prototype.sort comparator return?
What if req.body.apiKey is an object instead of a string?

title: Payments: Idempotency & Double Charges
tagline: Mobile retries charge customers twice, and $19.99 becomes 1998.9999 cents.
ticket:
**PAY-911 · SEV-2 · Customers double charged**

The mobile client retries `POST /api/payments` on timeouts and always sends an `Idempotency-Key` header. Customers are still being charged twice, sometimes even when two retries arrive **at the same time**. Finance also found charges with **fractional cents**.

Requirements: same key ⇒ exactly one charge; replays return **200** with the original body; amounts are stored as **integer cents**.

bugs.title: header lookup is case-sensitive
bugs.explain: Node lowercases incoming header names. `req.headers['Idempotency-Key']` is always undefined. Use `req.get('Idempotency-Key')` or the lowercase key.

bugs.title: race between check and set
bugs.explain: Both concurrent requests pass `responses.has(key)` before either finishes `await charge()`. Store the **in-flight promise** before awaiting, so the second request awaits the same one.

bugs.title: floating-point cents
bugs.explain: `19.99 * 100 === 1998.9999999999998`. Use `Math.round(amount * 100)`. Money should be integers in the smallest unit.

hints: Log Object.keys(req.headers).
Between `responses.has` and `responses.set` there is an `await`. What can happen during it?
Type 19.99 * 100 in a JS console.

title: Retry with Exponential Backoff
tagline: The retry helper gives up early, waits wrong, and swallows errors.
ticket:
**INFRA-58 · Outage amplified by our own retry helper**

During yesterday's database throttling event, callers using `lib/retry.js` saw `undefined` results instead of errors, retried **400 Bad Request** responses in a hot loop, and backed off linearly instead of exponentially.

The intended contract is in the doc comment. This is a **unit-test** lab: no HTTP involved.

bugs.title: loop bound off by two
bugs.explain: `attempt < retries` with attempt starting at 1 makes `retries - 1` attempts. The contract is `1 + retries`, so `attempt <= retries + 1`.

bugs.title: linear instead of exponential backoff
bugs.explain: `base * 2 * attempt` gives 200, 400, 600. Exponential is `base * 2 ** (attempt - 1)`.

bugs.title: final error swallowed
bugs.explain: After the loop the function falls off the end and returns `undefined`. `throw lastErr`.

bugs.title: retries non-retryable errors and sleeps after the last attempt
bugs.explain: Rethrow immediately when `err.retryable === false`, and break before sleeping on the final attempt.

hints: Count attempts for retries = 3 by hand.
What does an async function return if it reaches the end without `return`?
Write the expected delay sequence next to the formula.

title: Notification Fan-out
tagline: One bad device token kills the whole campaign; every greeting says 'Hi undefined'.
ticket:
**MKT-204 · Peak-sale campaign only partially sent**

The campaign job crashed with `no device token` and **nobody** got a report of what was delivered. The deferred greeting tasks also produce `"Hi undefined, …"` for every customer.

`notifyAll` must deliver everything it can and **report** failures (see doc comment).

bugs.title: Promise.all fails fast
bugs.explain: `Promise.all` rejects as soon as one promise rejects, so you lose all the other outcomes. Use `Promise.allSettled` and build the report from each result.

bugs.title: `var` in a loop with closures
bugs.explain: `var i` is function-scoped. Every closure sees the final `i === users.length`, so `users[i]` is undefined. Use `let` (block scoped per iteration).

hints: What does Promise.all do when one of 5 promises rejects?
When do the greeting functions actually run, and what is `i` then?

title: LRU Cache Gone Wrong
tagline: It evicts the newest item and never actually remembers anything.
ticket:
**PERF-17 · Hot-item cache hit rate is 0%**

The catalogue team's in-process LRU cache reports **0 hits** in production and seems to throw away whatever was just inserted. The contract is in the class doc comment.

bugs.title: `this.map[key]` on a Map
bugs.explain: Map entries aren't properties. `map[key]` is always undefined. Use `map.has(key)`. Also, a truthiness check would treat 0 as a miss.

bugs.title: get() doesn't refresh recency
bugs.explain: A Map iterates in insertion order. Delete and re-set the key to move it to the 'most recent' end.

bugs.title: evicts newest, and too early
bugs.explain: Evict when `size > capacity` (not `>=`), and evict the **first** key: `map.keys().next().value`.

bugs.title: put() on an existing key
bugs.explain: Delete first so the update moves the key to the most-recent position.

hints: Is `new Map()` indexable with brackets?
In which order does a Map iterate its keys?
With capacity 2, after the 2nd put should anything be evicted?

title: Payment Webhook Receiver
tagline: Every webhook is rejected, forged ones get through, and paid orders show as refunded.
ticket:
**PAY-310 · Payment provider is disabling our webhook endpoint**

The provider's dashboard shows **100% failures** for `POST /webhooks/payments` and threatens to disable it. Their docs:

- Each delivery has `x-signature: t=<unix seconds>,v1=<digest>` (see `lib/signature.js`). Reject a bad digest or a timestamp more than **5 minutes** away with **401**.
- Respond **2xx** to every authentic event, **including types you don't handle**. Anything else is retried with backoff for 3 days.

Security also found that a request with a garbage signature **still updated an order**. And on the rare day something got through, paid orders showed as **refunded**.

The webhook secret is `process.env.WEBHOOK_SECRET`.

bugs.title: milliseconds vs seconds
bugs.explain: `Date.now()` is in **milliseconds**; the header's `t` is in **seconds**. The difference is always about 1.7 trillion, so every event looked stale. Compare `Date.now() / 1000` with `Number(t)`.

bugs.title: missing return after 401
bugs.explain: Without `return`, the middleware sends 401 **and then calls `next()`**, so the handler still runs and updates the order. In real Express this also triggers "headers already sent".

bugs.title: switch fall-through
bugs.explain: `case 'payment.succeeded'` has no `break`, so execution falls into the refunded case and overwrites `paid` with `refunded`.

bugs.title: non-2xx for unknown events
bugs.explain: Providers retry any non-2xx. Acknowledge events you don't handle with 200, or one new event type fills your logs and gets the endpoint disabled.

hints: Log `Date.now()` next to the header's t value.
After `res.status(401).json(...)`, what runs next?
Read the switch statement aloud. Where does the first case stop?

title: Monthly Sales Report
tagline: March shows up as February, the last day of the month vanishes, and averages are tiny.
ticket:
**FIN-88 · Finance doesn't trust the dashboard**

The sales report (`GET /api/reports/sales?from=…&to=…&by=day|month`) disagrees with the bank statement:

- The March report is labelled **2024-02**.
- Sales on **the last day** of a range are missing (`to` is meant to be inclusive).
- **Cancelled** sales are counted as revenue.
- The average sale per day is far too small on busy reports.

Everything is in UTC. Amounts are integer cents.

bugs.title: zero-based month
bugs.explain: `getUTCMonth()` returns 0–11. Add 1 before formatting.

bugs.title: average divides by the wrong count
bugs.explain: Each bucket's average must divide by **that bucket's** count, not by the number of sales in the whole report.

bugs.title: inclusive end date at midnight
bugs.explain: `new Date('2024-03-31')` is **00:00** on the 31st, so `$lte` drops everything later that day. Use `$lt` with the start of the **next** day.

bugs.title: cancelled sales counted
bugs.explain: Filter on `status: 'completed'` in the query.

hints: What does `new Date(2024, 0, 1).getMonth()` return?
A date string with no time is which instant?
Compute the average of one bucket by hand.

title: Python: Bank Ledger Integrity
tagline: Every account shares one history, and money vanishes in failed transfers.
ticket:
**FIN-12 · Ledger audit failed**

Auditors found three problems in `bank/ledger.py`:

1. Opening a new account shows **other customers' transactions** in its history (and tags).
2. Balances drift: `0.1 + 0.2` shows as `0.30000000000000004`.
3. A transfer to an unknown account **debited the sender** anyway, and someone withdrew a **negative** amount to mint money.

Make `tests/test_ledger.py` pass. This is plain Python (`unittest`).

tests.tests/test_ledger.py:
import unittest
from decimal import Decimal

from bank.ledger import Account, transfer, InsufficientFunds


class LedgerTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_balances_are_exact_decimals(self):
        """0.1 + 0.2 must be exactly 0.3"""
        a = Account("ana")
        a.deposit("0.1")
        a.deposit("0.2")
        self.assertEqual(a.balance, Decimal("0.3"))

    def test_history_is_per_account(self):
        a, b = Account("ana"), Account("bo")
        a.deposit(5)
        self.assertEqual(len(a.history), 1)
        self.assertEqual(b.history, [])

    def test_tags_are_not_shared(self):
        a, b = Account("ana"), Account("bo")
        self.assertEqual(a.tags, ["new"])
        self.assertEqual(b.tags, ["new"])

    def test_cannot_withdraw_negative(self):
        a = Account("ana", 10)
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            a.withdraw(-5)
        self.assertEqual(a.balance, Decimal("10"))

    def test_insufficient_funds(self):
        a = Account("ana", 10)
        with self.assertRaises(InsufficientFunds):
            a.withdraw(11)

    def test_transfer_is_atomic_on_bad_destination(self):
        a = Account("ana", 50)
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            transfer(a, None, 20)
        self.assertEqual(a.balance, Decimal("50"))

    def test_transfer_moves_money(self):
        a, b = Account("ana", 50), Account("bo")
        transfer(a, b, "12.35")
        self.assertEqual((a.balance, b.balance), (Decimal("37.65"), Decimal("12.35")))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

bugs.title: class attribute shared by all instances
bugs.explain: `history = []` at class level is **one list** shared by every Account. Create it in `__init__` as `self.history = []`.

bugs.title: mutable default argument
bugs.explain: `tags=[]` is evaluated **once** when the function is defined, so every call shares it. Use `tags=None` and create a new list.

bugs.title: floats for money
bugs.explain: Binary floats can't represent 0.1 exactly. Use `Decimal(str(x))`, which also accepts ints and strings.

bugs.title: validation after side effects
bugs.explain: Validate everything (destination, positive amount) **before** mutating state. Otherwise a failure leaves a half-done transfer.

hints: Where does `history` live: the instance or the class?
When is a default argument value created in Python?
What happens to src.balance if dst is None?

title: Python: Token Bucket Rate Limiter
tagline: One noisy client throttles everyone, and limits never recover.
ticket:
**API-77 · Throttling misbehaves**

- Client **A** hammering the API also gets **client B** throttled.
- After a client is throttled, it stays blocked far longer than the configured rate allows.
- With `rate=2` tokens/s, waiting 0.5s should give exactly one more request.
- After a long idle period, clients get a burst **bigger than capacity**.

bugs.title: dict.fromkeys shares one object
bugs.explain: `dict.fromkeys(keys, value)` puts the **same** TokenBucket under every key. Use a dict comprehension to create one per client.

bugs.title: spending before checking (token debt)
bugs.explain: Decrementing first lets rejected calls push tokens negative, so the client must 'repay' before it recovers. Check `tokens >= 1`, then spend.

bugs.title: floor division drops fractional refill
bugs.explain: `elapsed // 1` truncates 0.5s to 0. Use `elapsed * rate`.

bugs.title: no capacity cap
bugs.explain: Clamp with `min(capacity, …)` so idle time can't build an unbounded burst.

hints: What does `dict.fromkeys(['a','b'], X())` do with X()?
What is `0.5 // 1`?
Should a *rejected* call cost a token?

title: Python: Access-Log Analyzer
tagline: The on-call dashboard crashes on empty logs and miscounts errors.

files.logs/analyzer.py:
import re
from collections import Counter

# 2026-01-15T10:00:01Z GET /api/orders 200 123ms
LINE = re.compile(r"^(\S+) (\S+) (\S+) (\d{3}) (\d+)ms$")


def parse(lines):
    for raw in lines:
        m = LINE.match(raw)
        if not m:
            continue
        ts, method, path, status, ms = m.groups()
        yield {"method": method, "path": path, "status": status, "ms": int(ms)}


def report(lines, top=2):
    """Summary of an access log.

    - top_paths: the `top` most requested paths as (path, count), ties broken alphabetically
    - error_rate: % of requests with status >= 500, rounded to 1 decimal
    - p_slowest: the slowest request time in ms
    - total: number of valid lines
    """
    entries = parse(lines)
    counts = Counter(e["path"] for e in entries)
    total = sum(counts.values())
    errors = sum(1 for e in entries if e["status"] >= "500")
    slowest = max(e["ms"] for e in entries)
    return {
        "top_paths": counts.most_common(top),
        "error_rate": round(errors / total * 100) if total else 0.0,
        "p_slowest": slowest,
        "total": total,
    }

import re
from collections import Counter

# 2026-01-15T10:00:01Z GET /api/orders 200 123ms
LINE = re.compile(r"^(\S+)\s+(\S+)\s+(\S+)\s+(\d{3})\s+(\d+)ms\s*$")


def parse(lines):
    for raw in lines:
        m = LINE.match(raw.strip())
        if not m:
            continue
        ts, method, path, status, ms = m.groups()
        yield {"method": method, "path": path, "status": int(status), "ms": int(ms)}


def report(lines, top=2):
    """Summary of an access log.

    - top_paths: the `top` most requested paths as (path, count), ties broken alphabetically
    - error_rate: % of requests with status >= 500, rounded to 1 decimal
    - p_slowest: the slowest request time in ms
    - total: number of valid lines
    """
    entries = list(parse(lines))
    counts = Counter(e["path"] for e in entries)
    total = len(entries)
    errors = sum(1 for e in entries if e["status"] >= 500)
    slowest = max((e["ms"] for e in entries), default=0)
    ranked = sorted(counts.items(), key=lambda kv: (-kv[1], kv[0]))
    return {
        "top_paths": ranked[:top],
        "error_rate": round(errors / total * 100, 1) if total else 0.0,
        "p_slowest": slowest,
        "total": total,
    }

bugs.title: generator consumed more than once
bugs.explain: `parse()` returns a generator. The first `Counter(...)` exhausts it, so later passes see **nothing** (`max()` of empty → ValueError). Materialise with `list(...)`.

bugs.title: comparing status codes as strings
bugs.explain: `'1000' >= '500'` is False and `'60' >= '500'` is True: string comparison is lexicographic. Convert to `int`.

bugs.title: regex too strict about whitespace
bugs.explain: Single literal spaces fail on `GET  /api/cart`. Use `\\s+`.

bugs.title: rounding & tie-breaking
bugs.explain: `round(x)` → int. Use `round(x, 1)`. `most_common` keeps insertion order on ties, so sort by `(-count, path)` explicitly. Use `max(..., default=0)` for empty input.

hints: How many times can you iterate a generator?
Compare '1000' >= '500' in a Python shell.
What does round(16.666) return?

title: Python: Meeting Scheduler

**CAL-8 · "Find a time" suggests busy slots**

Calendar sync passes busy intervals **unsorted**. The free-slot finder then suggests times that are already booked, misses 30-minute slots when `min_len=30`, and `drop_cancelled` leaves some cancelled meetings behind.

bugs.title: merge assumes sorted input

Is a 30-minute gap a valid 30-minute slot?

title: Python: TTL Cache Decorator
tagline: EUR prices come back in USD and None is never cached.
ticket:
**PRC-5 · Pricing cache returns wrong currency**

`@ttl_cache` wraps the pricing lookup. Customers in Europe see **USD prices** after a US customer views the same SKU. Lookups that return `None` hit the database every time, and our tracing shows every cached function named `wrapper`.

files.util/memo.py:
import time


def ttl_cache(seconds, clock=time.monotonic):
    """Cache results per (args, kwargs) for `seconds`. Exposes .cache_clear() and keeps
    the wrapped function's __name__ and __doc__."""

    def decorator(fn):
        store = {}

        def wrapper(*args, **kwargs):
            key = args
            hit = store.get(key)
            if hit and hit[0] and clock() - hit[1] < seconds:
                return hit[0]
            value = fn(*args, **kwargs)
            store[key] = (value, clock())
            return value

        wrapper.cache_clear = store.clear
        return wrapper

    return decorator

bugs.title: cache key ignores kwargs
bugs.explain: `key = args` makes `price('a', currency='EUR')` collide with `price('a')`. Include `tuple(sorted(kwargs.items()))`.

bugs.title: truthiness check on the cached value
bugs.explain: `hit[0] and …` treats cached `None`, `0`, `''` or `[]` as a miss, so those lookups hit the DB every time. Check presence with `hit is not None`, never the value's truthiness.

bugs.title: missing functools.wraps
bugs.explain: Decorators replace the function object. `@functools.wraps(fn)` copies `__name__`, `__doc__` and more.

hints: Print the cache key for price('a', currency='EUR').
What does a decorator return, and what's its __name__?

**Why it matters:** rate limiting shows up constantly, both in "build an API" tasks and in system-design follow-ups. You'll need per-key state in a closure, time math, and correct HTTP semantics (`429`, `Retry-After`).

title: Build: Concurrent Job Queue
tagline: A promise queue with a concurrency limit, retries, stats and onIdle().
ticket:
## Spec

Implement `createQueue` in `lib/queue.js` (contract in the doc comment). This is the pattern behind upload managers, crawlers and background workers.

**Key ideas:** keep a FIFO array of `{ task, resolve, reject }`; a `pump()` function starts tasks while `running < concurrency`; when a task settles, decrement `running` and pump again.

bugs.title: Wrap each task in a promise
bugs.explain: `add(task)` returns `new Promise((resolve, reject) => { waiting.push({ task, resolve, reject }); pump(); })`.

bugs.title: pump()
bugs.explain: `while (running < concurrency && waiting.length)`: shift a job, `running++`, run it, and in `finally` do `running--; pump();`.

bugs.title: Retries
bugs.explain: Loop `attempt = 0..retries`, return on success, remember the error, and throw the last one at the end.

bugs.title: onIdle + stats
bugs.explain: Keep a list of idle resolvers and flush it when `running === 0 && waiting.length === 0`.

hints: You can store a Promise's resolve function and call it later.
When should pump() run? On add AND whenever a task finishes.
Count done/failed in the then/catch handlers.

- **mutating the listener array while iterating it** (a `once` listener removes itself mid-emit)

/**
 * A tiny EventEmitter.
 *
 * on(event, fn)    subscribe; returns an unsubscribe function
 * once(event, fn)  subscribe for the next emit only
 * off(event, fn)   unsubscribe (works for once-listeners too, using the original fn)
 * emit(event, ...args) call listeners in subscription order; returns true if there were any
 *   - a listener that throws must not stop the others; collect errors and, after all
 *     listeners ran, emit them on the 'error' event (or rethrow the first if nobody listens to 'error')
 * listenerCount(event)
 */

  // TODO
}

bugs.explain: `Map<event, Array<{ fn, original }>>`. Keep the original so `off(event, original)` can find wrapped once-listeners.

title: Build (Python): Transactional Key-Value Store
tagline: set/get/delete/count with nested BEGIN, ROLLBACK and COMMIT.
ticket:
## Spec

Implement `KVStore` in `store/kv.py`. Contract in the docstring.

This is a well-known take-home and onsite problem. The elegant solution keeps an **undo log per open transaction**: before the first write to a key inside a transaction, remember its previous value. Rollback replays the top undo log. Keep `count` **O(1)** with a value → count map.

tests.tests/test_kv.py:
import unittest

from store.kv import KVStore


class BasicTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_set_get_delete(self):
        s = KVStore()
        s.set("a", 10)
        self.assertEqual(s.get("a"), 10)
        s.delete("a")
        self.assertIsNone(s.get("a"))

    def test_count_tracks_values(self):
        s = KVStore()
        s.set("a", 10); s.set("b", 10); s.set("b", 20)
        self.assertEqual((s.count(10), s.count(20), s.count(99)), (1, 1, 0))


class TransactionTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_rollback_restores_previous_values(self):
        s = KVStore()
        s.set("a", 1)
        s.begin()
        s.set("a", 2); s.set("b", 3); s.delete("a")
        s.rollback()
        self.assertEqual((s.get("a"), s.get("b")), (1, None))
        self.assertEqual(s.count(1), 1)

    def test_nested_rollback_only_undoes_inner(self):
        s = KVStore()
        s.begin(); s.set("a", 1)
        s.begin(); s.set("a", 2)
        s.rollback()
        self.assertEqual(s.get("a"), 1)
        s.rollback()
        self.assertIsNone(s.get("a"))

    def test_commit_closes_all_transactions(self):
        s = KVStore()
        s.begin(); s.set("a", 1); s.begin(); s.set("a", 2)
        s.commit()
        self.assertEqual(s.get("a"), 2)
        with self.assertRaisesRegex(RuntimeError, "NO TRANSACTION"):
            s.rollback()

    def test_errors_without_transaction(self):
        s = KVStore()
        with self.assertRaises(RuntimeError):
            s.commit()

    def test_counts_after_rollback(self):
        s = KVStore()
        s.set("x", "v")
        s.begin(); s.set("y", "v"); s.set("x", "w")
        self.assertEqual(s.count("v"), 1)
        s.rollback()
        self.assertEqual((s.count("v"), s.count("w")), (1, 0))

bugs.title: Core state
bugs.explain: `data` dict, `counts` dict (value → number of keys), and `undo_stack` (list of dicts).

bugs.title: Single write path
bugs.explain: Route set and delete through one `_write` that records the old value (once per key per transaction) and keeps `counts` in sync.

bugs.title: rollback / commit
bugs.explain: Rollback pops the top undo dict and restores each key; commit just clears the stack. Both raise when the stack is empty.

hints: Use a sentinel object to remember 'key did not exist'.
Only record the FIRST old value for a key per transaction.

title: Build (Python): Parking Lot OOD
tagline: The most famous object-oriented design question, implemented and tested.
ticket:
## Spec

Implement `ParkingLot` in `lot/parking.py` (contract in the docstring).

Design-round follow-ups to think about while you code: how would you support **multiple floors**, **pricing**, **reservations**, or **concurrent gates**? A min-heap of free spots per size gives O(log n) park/leave.

files.lot/parking.py:
from enum import IntEnum


class Size(IntEnum):
    MOTORCYCLE = 1
    CAR = 2
    VAN = 3


class ParkingLot:
    """Object-oriented parking lot.

    ParkingLot({Size.MOTORCYCLE: 2, Size.CAR: 3, Size.VAN: 1})  spots per size

    park(plate, size) -> spot id like "CAR-0"; a vehicle takes the SMALLEST free spot that fits
                         (a spot fits if spot size >= vehicle size), lowest index first.
                         Returns None if no spot fits. Parking an already-parked plate raises ValueError.
    leave(plate)      -> the freed spot id; KeyError if the plate isn't parked
    available(size)   -> number of free spots of exactly that size
    where(plate)      -> spot id or None
    """

    def __init__(self, spots):
        pass  # TODO

    def park(self, plate, size):
        raise NotImplementedError

    def leave(self, plate):
        raise NotImplementedError

    def available(self, size):
        raise NotImplementedError

    def where(self, plate):
        raise NotImplementedError

tests.tests/test_parking.py:
import unittest

from lot.parking import ParkingLot, Size


def lot():
    return ParkingLot({Size.MOTORCYCLE: 1, Size.CAR: 2, Size.VAN: 1})


class ParkingTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_vehicle_takes_matching_size(self):
        p = lot()
        self.assertEqual(p.park("C1", Size.CAR), "CAR-0")
        self.assertEqual(p.park("M1", Size.MOTORCYCLE), "MOTORCYCLE-0")

    def test_falls_back_to_next_bigger_spot(self):
        p = lot()
        p.park("M1", Size.MOTORCYCLE)
        self.assertEqual(p.park("M2", Size.MOTORCYCLE), "CAR-0")

    def test_never_uses_smaller_spot(self):
        p = lot()
        p.park("V1", Size.VAN)
        self.assertIsNone(p.park("V2", Size.VAN))

    def test_lowest_free_index_is_reused(self):
        p = lot()
        p.park("A", Size.CAR); p.park("B", Size.CAR)
        self.assertEqual(p.leave("A"), "CAR-0")
        self.assertEqual(p.park("C", Size.CAR), "CAR-0")

    def test_available_counts(self):
        p = lot()
        p.park("A", Size.CAR)
        self.assertEqual((p.available(Size.CAR), p.available(Size.VAN)), (1, 1))

    def test_double_park_and_unknown_leave(self):
        p = lot()
        p.park("A", Size.CAR)
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            p.park("A", Size.CAR)
        with self.assertRaises(KeyError):
            p.leave("ZZZ")

    def test_where(self):
        p = lot()
        p.park("A", Size.VAN)
        self.assertEqual(p.where("A"), "VAN-0")
        self.assertIsNone(p.where("B"))

bugs.title: Free-spot structure
bugs.explain: One min-heap of free indices per size: `heapq.heappop` always yields the lowest free index.

bugs.title: Best-fit search
bugs.explain: Iterate sizes ascending, take the first size ≥ vehicle size that still has a free spot.

bugs.title: Bookkeeping
bugs.explain: `parked: plate → (size, index)` powers `leave`, `where` and the duplicate check.

hints: IntEnum members compare like ints.
heapq turns a list into a priority queue in place.

title: Build (Python): In-Memory File System
tagline: mkdir -p, append-writes, ls, rm -r and du on a tree of nodes.
ticket:
## Spec

Implement `FileSystem` in `fs/memfs.py` (contract in the docstring).

The core idea is a **trie of path segments**: each node has `children: dict`, `is_file` and `content`. Most methods are "walk the path, then do one thing". `du` is a recursive sum.

tests.tests/test_memfs.py:
import unittest

from fs.memfs import FileSystem


class FsTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.fs = FileSystem()

    def test_mkdir_creates_parents_and_ls_sorts(self):
        self.fs.mkdir("/a/b/c")
        self.fs.mkdir("/a/aa")
        self.assertEqual(self.fs.ls("/a"), ["aa", "b"])
        self.assertEqual(self.fs.ls("/"), ["a"])

    def test_write_creates_and_appends(self):
        self.fs.write("/logs/app.log", "hello")
        self.fs.write("/logs/app.log", " world")
        self.assertEqual(self.fs.read("/logs/app.log"), "hello world")

    def test_ls_on_file(self):
        self.fs.write("/x/readme.md", "#")
        self.assertEqual(self.fs.ls("/x/readme.md"), ["readme.md"])

    def test_read_errors(self):
        self.fs.mkdir("/d")
        with self.assertRaises(FileNotFoundError):
            self.fs.read("/nope.txt")
        with self.assertRaises(IsADirectoryError):
            self.fs.read("/d")

    def test_rm_recursive(self):
        self.fs.write("/a/b/f.txt", "123")
        self.fs.rm("/a/b")
        self.assertEqual(self.fs.ls("/a"), [])
        with self.assertRaises(FileNotFoundError):
            self.fs.rm("/a/b")

    def test_du(self):
        self.fs.write("/p/one.txt", "12345")
        self.fs.write("/p/q/two.txt", "abc")
        self.assertEqual((self.fs.du("/p"), self.fs.du("/p/q"), self.fs.du("/")), (8, 3, 8))

bugs.title: Node model
bugs.explain: A small `Node` class with `children`, `is_file`, `content`. The root is a directory node.

bugs.title: One _walk helper

bugs.explain: write = walk(parent, create) + setdefault file + append; rm = delete from the parent's children; du = recursive sum.
